output.answer: Most recently, Bayer’s 2025 Annual Report says Monsanto announced in February 2026 a proposed U.S. nationwide class settlement for current and future Roundup glyphosate claims; it was still awaiting preliminary approval, so this is a post-acquisition litigation development rather than a change to the transaction itself. Bayer completed the all-cash acquisition of 100% of Monsanto on June 7, 2018: shareholders received $128 per share, Monsanto ceased trading, and Bayer became its sole owner; Bayer reported the transaction value as $63 billion including Monsanto’s debt. Regulatory approval required major remedies—more than €6 billion in commitments under the European Commission’s review, including divestitures of overlapping seed, trait and pesticide businesses and licensing of Bayer’s digital-agriculture portfolio, principally to BASF—after which integration began in August 2018.
caveats: The 2026 Roundup class settlement was described as proposed and subject to a motion for preliminary approval; the source does not establish that final court approval had occurred as of the report.

The transaction is commonly described as a roughly US$63 billion acquisition including debt; the shareholder consideration was specifically US$128 per share, not US$63 billion in cash paid directly to shareholders.

key_facts.fact: In February 2026, Monsanto announced a proposed U.S. nationwide class settlement for current and future Roundup glyphosate claims; plaintiff counsel filed a motion seeking preliminary approval.

The European Commission approved the acquisition subject to remedies worth well over €6 billion, covering overlaps in seeds and pesticides, Bayer seed-and-trait R&D, certain Monsanto assets, and licensing of Bayer’s global digital-agriculture portfolio.
